summary: The @gyomu/config package serves as the centralized configuration management system for the application. It orchestrates the retrieval, validation, and hierarchical merging of configuration settings from multiple sources into a strongly typed, environment-aware result.
responsibilities: Define a hierarchical resolution strategy that merges global, user, and scope-based configurations.
Enforce schema-based validation on resolved configuration objects.
Provide a unified service-based API for accessing configuration values within the application.
Manage the lifecycle of the configuration resolution process, including state and phase tracking.
Centralize error handling for configuration retrieval failures with metadata for diagnostic and recovery purposes.

capabilities.name: Configuration Resolution
capabilities.description: Orchestrates the multi-layered retrieval of settings by applying precedence rules across global, user, and scope definitions.

capabilities.name: Typed Configuration Access
capabilities.description: Exposes a service interface that delivers validated and type-safe configuration data to application components.

capabilities.name: Resolution Diagnostics
capabilities.description: Provides structured error context to help developers troubleshoot and identify failure points during the configuration lookup process.

designDecisions: Utilizes the Effect ecosystem to represent the configuration resolution as a modular and injectable service.
Adopts a query-based approach to configuration lookup, allowing consumers to specify filtering criteria like scope and function context.
Implements a clear distinction between resolution phases and error contexts to support reliable observability and retry logic.
usageGuidance: Inject the ConfigResolver service via the Effect dependency injection system to access configuration within your modules.
Define your resolution requirements using the ConfigQuery object to target specific scopes or functions as needed.
Handle configuration resolution errors by inspecting the provided error context to determine if a operation should be retried or if the failure is terminal.
